claim: Male mice produce ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) during courtship to facilitate mating.
source: Male mice produce ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) during courtship to facilitate mating
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the field, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Previously isolated female mice produce USVs during social encounters with novel females.
source: previously isolated female mice produce USVs during social encounters with novel females
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data and citations to prior work.

claim: PAG-USV neurons are an obligatory gate for USV production in both male and female mice.
source: a specialized set of neurons in the midbrain periaqueductal gray (PAG-USV neurons) are an obligatory gate for USV production in both male and female mice
evidence: This is based on prior work by the authors (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: PAG-USV neurons can be switched on by their inputs from the preoptic area (POA) of the hypothalamus.
source: both PAG-USV neurons and USVs can be switched on by their inputs from the preoptic area (POA) of the hypothalamus
evidence: This is based on prior work by the authors (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: PAG-USV neurons can be switched off by their inputs from neurons on the border between the central and medial amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons).
source: both PAG-USV neurons and USVs can be switched on by their inputs from the preoptic area (POA) of the hypothalamus and switched off by their inputs from neurons on the border between the central and medial amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) (Michael et al., 2020)
evidence: This is based on prior work by the authors (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons are strongly activated by predator cues in male and female mice.
source: the USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons are strongly activated by predator cues or during social contexts that suppress USV production in male and female mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons are strongly activated during social contexts that suppress USV production in male and female mice.
source: the USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons are strongly activated by predator cues or during social contexts that suppress USV production in male and female mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons receive monosynaptic inhibitory input from POA neurons that also project to the PAG.
source: AmgC/M-PAG neurons receive monosynaptic inhibitory input from POA neurons that also project to the PAG
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by rabies tracing and electrophysiology data.

claim: Inhibitory inputs from POA to AmgC/M-PAG neurons are active in USV-promoting social contexts.
source: these inhibitory inputs are active in USV-promoting social contexts
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: Optogenetic activation of POA cell bodies that make divergent axonal projections to the amygdala and PAG is sufficient to elicit USV production in socially isolated male mice.
source: optogenetic activation of POA cell bodies that make divergent axonal projections to the amygdala and PAG is sufficient to elicit USV production in socially isolated male mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic experiments.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons, along with POAPAG and PAG-USV neurons, form a nested hierarchical circuit in which environmental and social information converges to influence the decision to vocalize.
source: AmgC/M-PAG neurons, along with POAPAG and PAG-USV neurons, form a nested hierarchical circuit in which environmental and social information converges to influence the decision to vocalize
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, integrating multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Vocalizations help foster mating and social bonding in most mammals.
source: Vocalizations help foster mating and social bonding in most mammals (Seyfarth and Cheney, 2010)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Vocalizing in the wrong context can increase the risk of attracting the attention of eavesdropping predators or social rivals.
source: vocalizing in the wrong context can increase the risk of attracting the attention of eavesdropping predators or social rivals (Akre et al., 2011; Roberts et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Male mice produce USVs robustly to females to facilitate mating.
source: when presented with females, male mice produce USVs robustly to females to facilitate mating (Chabout et al., 2015; Neunuebel et al., 2015; Portfors, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: After being subjected to social isolation, resident female mice start to produce significantly more USVs in response to a novel female.
source: a recent study by Zhao et al., 2021 showed that after being subjected to social isolation, resident female mice start to produce significantly more USVs in response to a novel female
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work (Zhao et al., 2021).

claim: PAG-USV neurons serve as an obligatory gate for USV production.
source: The recent identification of neurons in the midbrain periaqueductal gray (PAG) that serve as an obligatory gate for USV production (PAG-USV neurons) provides the potential for understanding the circuit logic underlying a mouse's decision to vocalize (Tschida et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work (Tschida et al., 2019).

claim: A GABAergic projection from the hypothalamic preoptic area (POA) to the PAG drives USV production in male and female mice in part through disynaptic disinhibition of PAG-USV neurons.
source: a GABAergic projection from the hypothalamic preoptic area (POA) to the PAG drives USV production in male and female mice in part through disynaptic disinhibition of PAG-USV neurons (Chen et al., 2021; Michael et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A subpopulation of GABAergic neurons on the border of the central and medial amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) directly inhibits PAG-USV neurons.
source: a subpopulation of GABAergic neurons on the border of the central and medial amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) directly inhibits PAG-USV neurons
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: Optogenetically activating AmgC/M-PAG neurons in male mice suppresses their courtship USVs.
source: optogenetically activating these neurons in male mice suppresses their courtship USVs (Michael et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: POA neurons that express Estrogen receptor alpha (Esr1) are strongly activated in male mice during female courtship.
source: POA neurons that express Estrogen receptor alpha (Esr1), which is a molecular marker of POA neurons that innervate the PAG-USV region (Chen et al., 2021; Michael et al., 2020), are strongly activated in male mice during female courtship (Chen et al., 2021)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Some POA neurons that project to the PAG-USV region also project to the region of the amygdala that contains AmgC/M-PAG neurons.
source: some POA neurons that project to the PAG-USV region also project to the region of the amygdala that contains AmgC/M-PAG neurons (Michael et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work (Michael et al., 2020).

claim: Both male and female mice produced significantly fewer USVs when encounters with a novel female occurred in the presence of 2MT compared to controls.
source: We found that both male and female mice produced significantly fewer USVs when encounters with a novel female occurred in the presence of 2MT compared to controls (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1; Figure 1—video 2)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Calcium signals in AmgC/M-PAG neurons were significantly elevated above baseline when the animal approached and investigated dishes containing 2MT, a control odor (ethyl tiglate), a novel plastic 'toy', or the soiled bedding of male or female conspecifics.
source: In both sexes, calcium signals in AmgC/M-PAG neurons were significantly elevated above baseline when the animal approached and investigated dishes containing any of these items (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Calcium signals in AmgC/M-PAG neurons were the highest when investigating the dish containing 2MT.
source: they were the highest when investigating the dish containing 2MT (Figure 1D–F)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: The overall pattern of responsiveness to various stimuli was similar between male and female mice.
source: The overall pattern of responsiveness to these various stimuli was similar between male and female mice (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The calcium increase evoked by 2MT was not linked to subsequent bouts of freezing.
source: the calcium increase evoked by 2MT was not linked to subsequent bouts of freezing, suggesting that activity in these neurons was driven by detection of the odorant rather than the subsequent behavioral response (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: An innately aversive predator odorant suppresses USV production and strongly activates USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons in both male and female mice.
source: Therefore, an innately aversive predator odorant suppresses USV production and strongly activates USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons in both male and female mice
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral and fiber photometry data presented in the study.

claim: In both sexes, similar small increases in AmgC/M-PAG neuronal activity were observed when calcium signals were aligned to the onsets of non-aggressive social encounters with male or female conspecifics, or with a mouse's investigation of a novel object.
source: In both sexes, we observed similar small increases in AmgC/M-PAG neuronal activity when calcium signals were aligned to the onsets of non-aggressive social encounters with male or female conspecifics, or with a mouse's investigation of a novel object (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Calcium signals of AmgC/M-PAG neurons did not change significantly at the onset or offset of USV bouts.
source: However, calcium signals of AmgC/M-PAG neurons did not change significantly at the onset or offset of USV bouts, suggesting that AmgC/M-PAG neurons are not simply turning off USV bouts during non-aggressive social encounters (Figure 1H)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neuronal calcium signals increased markedly during aggressive interactions between two males that included attacks.
source: In contrast, AmgC/M-PAG neuronal calcium signals increased markedly during aggressive interactions between two males that included attacks (Figure 1I–J)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1I-J.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neuronal calcium signals were larger in the male being attacked.
source: Although many of these epochs included aggressive behavior from both males, AmgC/M-PAG neuronal calcium signals were larger in the male being attacked (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons exhibit large increases in activity during aggressive social encounters when USVs are not typically produced and much smaller increases in activity during affiliative social encounters in which USVs frequently occur.
source: In summary, AmgC/M-PAG neurons exhibit large increases in activity during aggressive social encounters when USVs are not typically produced and much smaller increases in activity during affiliative social encounters in which USVs frequently occur
evidence: This is a summary of the fiber photometry data presented in the study.

claim: While group-housed female mice produce few USVs in response to a novel female conspecific, previously isolated female mice produced significantly more USVs per minute, more USV bouts per minute, and longer USV bouts.
source: We observed that while group-housed female mice produce few USVs in response to a novel female conspecific, previously isolated female mice produced significantly more USVs per minute, more USV bouts per minute, and longer USV bouts, and in fact vocalized at rates comparable to isolated male mice during female presentation (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Previously isolated female mice vocalized at rates comparable to isolated male mice during female presentation.
source: previously isolated female mice produced significantly more USVs per minute, more USV bouts per minute, and longer USV bouts, and in fact vocalized at rates comparable to isolated male mice during female presentation (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of AmgC/M-PAG neurons in freely vocalizing female mice immediately suppressed USV production, and this suppression persisted throughout the duration of the laser pulse.
source: Optogenetic stimulation of AmgC/M-PAG neurons in freely vocalizing female mice immediately suppressed USV production, and this suppression persisted throughout the duration of the laser pulse (Figure 2C–D, N=5 of 5 female mice)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The optogenetically evoked decrease in USV rate was significant when compared to a light-only control condition, a control condition in which USV rates decreased naturally, and to a separate group of female mice in which GFP was expressed in AmgC/M-PAG neurons.
source: The optogenetically evoked decrease in USV rate was significant when compared to a light-only control condition in which the same mice were connected to a dummy ferrule that shone blue light above their heads, a control condition in which the same mice did not receive laser stimulation and USV rates decreased naturally, and to a separate group of female mice in which GFP was expressed in AmgC/M-PAG neurons and that were subjected to optical fiber illumination in the Amg (Figure 2D; Figure 2—video 1; N=5 female mice in the optogenetic condition, light control condition, and natural bout decay condition and N=5 female mice in the GFP control condition, p<0.01 for differences between ChR2 group vs. control groups during laser time; two-way ANOVA with repeated measures on one factor, p<0.01 for interaction between group and time, followed by post-hoc pairwise Tukey's HSD tests)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 2D and statistical analysis.

claim: After laser offset, the USV rate in the AmgC/M-PAG-ChR2 female mice rebounded to a level comparable to that in all control conditions.
source: After laser offset, the USV rate in the AmgC/M-PAG-ChR2 female mice rebounded to a level comparable to that in all control conditions (p>0.05 for differences between groups in post-laser period; Figure 2C–D)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 2C-D and statistical analysis.

claim: Vocal suppression by stimulating Amgc/m-PAG neurons in females was comparable to the previously reported vocal suppression by stimulating Amgc/m-PAG neurons in males.
source: When we compared these vocal suppression results to those reported in Michael et al., 2020, we found that vocal suppression by stimulating Amgc/m-PAG neurons in females was comparable to the previously reported vocal suppression by stimulating Amgc/m-PAG neurons in males (Michael et al., 2020; Figure 3H)
evidence: This is a comparison of the current study's findings with prior work, supported by data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: 100% of AmgC/M-PAG cells in female mice express VGAT (Slc32a1).
source: We used in situ hybridization to establish that 100% of AmgC/M-PAG cells in female mice express VGAT (Slc32a1), suggesting that they mediate USV suppression by directly inhibiting PAG-USV neurons (N=167/167 neurons in 2 female mice were VGAT+ (Slc32a1), and 0/167 were VGLUT2+ (Slc17a6); Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons are GABAergic and function to suppress vocalizations in female mice during social encounters with other females, similar to the manner in which these neurons suppress courtship USVs in male mice.
source: In summary, AmgC/M-PAG neurons are GABAergic and function to suppress vocalizations in female mice during social encounters with other females, similar to the manner in which these neurons suppress courtship USVs in male mice
evidence: This is a summary of the findings presented in the study.

claim: Nearly half of GFP-labeled AmgC/M-PAG neurons express Esr1.
source: We found that nearly half of GFP-labeled AmgC/M-PAG neurons express Esr1 (Figure 3B,~49%, N=913 cells from 7 mice, 3 males and 4 females; AmgC/M-PAG neurons labeled by injecting PAG with AAV-retro-Cre and amygdala with AAV-flex-GFP, similar to the strategy shown in Figure 2B)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Esr1+ amygdala cells send axonal projections to the region of caudolateral PAG, the region that contains PAG-USV neurons.
source: By injecting the amygdala of Esr1-cre mice with flex-tdTomato we further found that Esr1+ amygdala cells send axonal projections to the region of caudolateral PAG, the region that contains PAG-USV neurons, and consistent with our observation that a large subset of AmgC/M-PAG neurons are Esr1+ (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by anatomical tracing data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Optogenetic activation of Esr1+ AmgC/M cells immediately and reversibly suppressed USV production.
source: Optogenetic activation of Esr1+ AmgC/M cells immediately and reversibly suppressed USV production (N=9 mice; 5 males and 4 females; Figure 3E–G)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: Stimulation of Esr1+ AmgC/M neurons was specific to the time period of optogenetic stimulation and did not occur in light-only control conditions or in control conditions in which USV bouts were allowed to decay naturally.
source: As with stimulation of AmgC/M-PAG cells, this suppression was specific to the time period of optogenetic stimulation and did not occur in light-only control conditions or in control conditions in which USV bouts were allowed to decay naturally (Figure 3G; Figure 3—video 1; p<0.001 for differences between optogenetic condition and both control conditions during the laser stimulation period, two-way ANOVA followed by post-hoc pairwise Tukey's HSD tests)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 3G and statistical analysis.

claim: Stimulating either Esr1+ AmgC/M neurons or AmgC/M-PAG neurons reduced the USV rate (normalized to pre-laser baseline) to a comparable level.
source: Moreover, stimulating either Esr1+ AmgC/M neurons or AmgC/M-PAG neurons reduced the USV rate (normalized to pre-laser baseline) to a comparable level (Figure 3H)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Stimulating Esr1+ AmgC/M neurons was similarly efficient for suppressing USVs in both males and females.
source: Lastly, stimulating Esr1+ AmgC/M neurons was similarly efficient for suppressing USVs in both males and females
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data.

claim: Esr1+ AmgC/M-PAG neurons mediate vocal suppression in both male and female mice.
source: Taken together, this evidence suggests that Esr1+ AmgC/M-PAG neurons mediate vocal suppression in both male and female mice
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the optogenetic and anatomical data presented in the study.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons receive monosynaptic input from numerous cortical regions that process a wide variety of sensory and interoceptive information, including the piriform, motor, somatosensory, insular and auditory cortices.
source: This approach revealed that AmgC/M-PAG neurons in male mice receive monosynaptic input from numerous cortical regions that process a wide variety of sensory and interoceptive information, including the piriform, motor, somatosensory, insular and auditory cortices (Figure 4B; Bhattacharjee et al., 2021; Gogolla, 2017; Shipley and Ennis, 1996; Zatorre et al., 2002)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by rabies tracing data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons receive input from many other forebrain and midbrain regions, including the medial and lateral POA, the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the ventral tegmental area, and the nucleus accumbens shell.
source: We also observed that AmgC/M-PAG neurons receive input from many other forebrain and midbrain regions, including the medial and lateral POA, the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the ventral tegmental area, and the nucleus accumbens shell (Figure 4C–D)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by rabies tracing data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed a large and sustained increase at the onset of social interactions with female mice.
source: In contrast to the activity of AmgC/M-PAG neurons measured in these various conditions (Figure 1G), POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed a large and sustained increase at the onset of social interactions with female mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed a moderate sustained increase at the onset of non-aggressive social interactions with other male mice.
source: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed a large and sustained increase at the onset of social interactions with female mice, a moderate sustained increase at the onset of non-aggressive social interactions with other male mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed no response at the onset of or during trials where the mouse encountered a dish containing 2MT or a novel plastic toy.
source: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity showed a large and sustained increase at the onset of social interactions with female mice, a moderate sustained increase at the onset of non-aggressive social interactions with other male mice, and no response at the onset of or during trials where the mouse encountered a dish containing 2MT or a novel plastic toy (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity further increased at the onset of subsequent social interactions and at the onset of individual USV bouts.
source: In addition to the large and sustained increase in activity upon the introduction of a social partner, POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity further increased at the onset of subsequent social interactions and at the onset of individual USV bouts (Figure 5C–D)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity remained low when aligned to the onsets of the mouse's investigation of a dish containing 2MT or the onsets of attacks by male conspecifics.
source: However, POAEsr1-Amg terminal activity remained low when aligned to the onsets of the mouse's investigation of a dish containing 2MT or the onsets of attacks by male conspecifics (Figure 5E and F)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: POAEsr1-Amg axons in the AmgC/M-PAG of male mice are highly active during social encounters in which USVs are produced, but not in situations in which AmgC/M-PAG activity is high and USV production is suppressed.
source: Taken together, these findings support the idea that POAEsr1-Amg axons in the AmgC/M-PAG of male mice are highly active during social encounters in which USVs are produced, but not in situations in which AmgC/M-PAG activity is high and USV production is suppressed
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fiber photometry data presented in the study.

claim: The majority (~82%) of GFP-labeled POAAMG cells express Esr1.
source: We found that the majority (~82%) of GFP-labeled POAAMG cells express Esr1 (Figure 6B, N=298/362 cells from 2 male mice)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Axon terminals from GFP-labeled POAAMG cells were present in the caudolateral PAG, the same region where PAG-USV neurons are located.
source: We further noted that axon terminals from GFP-labeled POAAMG cells were present in the caudolateral PAG, the same region where PAG-USV neurons are located (Figure 6C, see also Tschida et al., 2019)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by anatomical tracing data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Exciting the cell bodies of ChR2-expressing POAAMG cells with blue light was sufficient to trigger USVs in male mice in the absence of social cues.
source: We found that exciting the cell bodies of these ChR2-expressing POAAMG cells with blue light was sufficient to trigger USVs in male mice in the absence of social cues (Figure 6E–G; Figure 6—video 1; N=4 male mice showed increased USV rates in response to this optogenetic stimulation)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data shown in Figure 6E-G.

claim: The effects on mean USV rate, success rate of eliciting USVs, and the mean latency to elicited USVs using the POAAMG optogenetic stimulation approach were not significantly different from the USV-promoting effects achieved by stimulating POAPAG neurons or Esr1+ POA terminals in PAG.
source: The effects on mean USV rate, success rate of eliciting USVs, and the mean latency to elicited USVs using the POAAMG optogenetic stimulation approach were not significantly different from the USV-promoting effects achieved by stimulating POAPAG neurons or Esr1+ POA terminals in PAG (Michael et al., 2020; Figure 6H)
evidence: This is a comparison of the current study's findings with prior work, supported by data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: The POA cells that convey pro-vocal social signals and USV-related signals to the AmgC/M are Esr1+ also project to the caudolateral PAG and directly promote USV production.
source: Therefore, the POA cells that convey pro-vocal social signals and USV-related signals to the AmgC/M are Esr1+ also project to the caudolateral PAG and directly promote USV production
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anatomical and optogenetic data presented in the study.

claim: Optogenetically activating POAPAG axon terminals in the amygdala evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) in a majority (9/13) of AmgC/M-PAG (td-Tomato+) neurons.
source: Optogenetically activating POAPAG axon terminals in the amygdala evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) in a majority (9/13) of AmgC/M-PAG (td-Tomato+) neurons (Figure 6J; mean current = 141.9 pA at 0 mV in TTX/4AP; currents with reversal potentials at –70 mV were identified as IPSCs, and no EPSCs were observed at –70 mV in the presence of TTX and 4AP)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Bath application of the GABAA receptor antagonist gabazine SR-95531 abolished these optogenetically evoked IPSCs in all four cases in which it was applied.
source: Bath application of the GABAA receptor antagonist gabazine SR-95531 abolished these optogenetically evoked IPSCs in all four cases in which it was applied (Figure 6J, 4/9 recordings)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: POAPAG cells provide monosynaptic inhibitory input onto AmgC/M-PAG neurons.
source: Therefore, POAPAG cells provide monosynaptic inhibitory input onto AmgC/M-PAG neurons
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiology data presented in the study.

claim: USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons, which are strongly activated by predator cues and social threats, are also directly inhibited by USV-promoting POA neurons.
source: These various findings support the idea that USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons, which are strongly activated by predator cues and social threats, are also directly inhibited by USV-promoting POA neurons
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anatomical, electrophysiological, and fiber photometry data presented in the study.

claim: Vocal-suppressing neurons in the amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) encode information about predators and threatening rivals.
source: Here, we provide evidence in mice that vocal-suppressing neurons in the amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) encode information about predators and threatening rivals
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: Vocal-suppressing neurons in the amygdala influence the decision to vocalize by integrating information about predators and threatening rivals with that about potential social partners and mates.
source: Here, we provide evidence in mice that vocal-suppressing neurons in the amygdala (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) encode information about predators and threatening rivals, and that they influence the decision to vocalize by integrating this information with that about potential social partners and mates
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, supported by anatomical, electrophysiological, and fiber photometry data.

claim: 2MT, a potent analog of the fox urine odorant TMT, suppresses USVs produced by male and female mice.
source: Using behavioral methods, we established that 2MT, a potent analog of the fox urine odorant TMT, suppresses USVs produced by male and female mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by behavioral data.

claim: PAG-projecting AmgC/M neurons (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) in both females and males were strongly activated during exposure to 2MT but not when the animal subsequently exhibited 2MT-evoked freezing or was exposed to other neutral odorants.
source: Moreover, using fiber photometric calcium imaging, we found that PAG-projecting AmgC/M neurons (AmgC/M-PAG neurons) in both females and males were strongly activated during exposure to 2MT but not when the animal subsequently exhibited 2MT-evoked freezing or was exposed to other neutral odorants
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by fiber photometry data.

claim: AmgC/M-PAG neurons provide a neural substrate for encoding threating social and environmental stimuli in either sex of mice.
source: These results indicate that AmgC/M-PAG neurons provide a neural substrate for encoding threating social and environmental stimuli in either sex of mice
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the fiber photometry data presented in the study.

claim: Stimulation of AmgC/M-PAG neurons not only suppresses USV production in male mice in the context of courtship but also operates similarly to suppress a form of social USV production in pairs of interacting female mice.
source: We showed that stimulation of AmgC/M-PAG neurons not only suppresses USV production in male mice in the context of courtship (Michael et al., 2020), but also operates similarly to suppress a form of social USV production in pairs of interacting female mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by optogenetic data.

claim: Although male and female mice produce USVs in different amounts and in different social and reproductive contexts, the amygdala >PAG pathway encodes information about interaction with threatening stimuli, and it functions similarly to effectively suppress vocalizations across contexts and in both sexes.
source: Thus, although male and female mice produce USVs in different amounts and in different social and reproductive contexts, the amygdala >PAG pathway encodes information about interaction with threatening stimuli, and it functions similarly to effectively suppress vocalizations across contexts and in both sexes
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, integrating multiple lines of evidence.

claim: USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons are predominantly GABAergic, with a subset expressing Esr1 in both female and male mice.
source: We also established that these USV-suppressing AmgC/M-PAG neurons are predominantly GABAergic, with a subset expressing Esr1 in both female and male mice
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry data.
